questions.question: List the eight parts of a data report in order, and write the method part for the transport investigation (300 Grade 9 learners, 60 sampled, 20 per class by every 15th name, anonymous two-item questionnaire during register).
questions.expected_answer: The parts are: the question as posed; the method; the organised data with table and graph; the summary statistics with reasons; the findings (conclusions and comparisons with numbers); the predictions with uncertainty; the limitations (error and bias with directions); and the recommendation. Method: the population was the 300 Grade 9 learners; a stratified sample of 60 was drawn, 20 from each of the three classes by taking every 15th name on each class list; data was collected with a two-item closed questionnaire on mode of transport and gender, completed anonymously during register on a Tuesday.

questions.question: From the two-way table (boys: walk 18, taxi 9, car 3; girls: walk 15, taxi 12, car 3), write two findings in the form claim, number, caution. Then predict the number of walkers among the 300 Grade 9 learners, showing the uncertainty.
questions.expected_answer: Finding 1: walking is the most common mode of transport; 33 of 60 learners, which is 55 percent, walk; as a sample of Grade 9 only, other grades may differ. Finding 2: girls are somewhat more likely than boys to use taxis; 12 of 30 girls, 40 percent, against 9 of 30 boys, 30 percent; the gap is three learners in thirty, so another sample could narrow it. Prediction: about 55 percent of 300, which is about 165 learners, walk to school; the word about is required because a sample of 60 cannot fix the population figure exactly, and extending to the whole school of 1200 would need the extra caution that only Grade 9 was sampled.

questions.question: The tuck shop spending data has a median of 12 rands, a mean of 17.25 and an outlier of 60. Explain how the report should present the typical spend and the outlier. Then write two limitations for the transport report, each with the direction in which it might push the findings.
questions.expected_answer: Report the median of 12 rands as the typical spend, because the outlier of 60 pulls the mean up to 17.25 while most learners spent between 8 and 20 rands; give the mean alongside with that explanation and give the range as 55, noting it is 20 without the outlier. State that the 60 was checked against the questionnaire, found to be genuine, kept in the data and its effect reported; it is neither silently removed nor silently included. Limitations: only Grade 9 was sampled, so predictions for the whole school assume other grades travel similarly and may be wrong in either direction; learners absent on the Tuesday may include those who travel furthest, so the walking percentage may be pushed slightly upward; also, random sampling error means another sample of 60 could give a figure several points from 55 percent.
